page.title: Gravatar to unread badges
page.kicker: Lecture 08 · week 4, day 2 · running case: Gravatar, photo tags, the unread badge
page.dek: Four small systems, each teaching one habit: images as route handlers, the query decides the design, the product hat, and pre-compute versus source of truth, ending with the auxiliary-database pattern.
page.description: Lecture 08: four small social-network systems, each teaching one habit: images as route handlers, the query decides the design, the product hat, and pre-compute versus source of truth.

chapters.title: Images are just responses
chapters.summary: “The image is served” hides a piece of code you could write yourself. Once you see the code, a URL can return an image that never existed until someone asked.

chapters.title: Gravatar: the query decides the design
chapters.summary: A system so simple you’d draw two boxes and stop. Write the exact queries and it changes three times: a stored hash, a transaction with an ownership check, and “active” moving to the user.

chapters.title: Serving Gravatar at every size
chapters.summary: Reuse the upload service, put a CDN in front of the API, tell the CDN when a photo changes, then let the same origin hand out any size on request.

chapters.title: Tagging: wear the product hat
chapters.summary: “Let’s allow people to tag people in photos.” One line from a CXO. Before any schema, ask the questions that decide who builds what.

chapters.title: The newly unread badge
chapters.summary: The small number on the messages icon. Pin down what it counts, build the correct but crude query, then replace it with a set kept up to date by the messaging service.

chapters.title: Protect the database: the auxiliary database
chapters.summary: The design works, but the database is doing work that changes nothing. Put a cheap store in front of it to absorb that work, and decide what inconsistency you can live with.

chapters.title: What to keep
chapters.summary: The habits that tie four small systems together, how to get good at query tuning, and where the course goes next.
